title: Precision Ocular Biometry: IOL Master vs. Ultrasound
summary: Mastering the shift from acoustic to optical biometry is fundamental for modern refractive cataract surgery. This guide compares gold-standard optical coherence interferometry with immersion A-scan ultrasound to optimize IOL power calculations.

sections.title: Indications for A-Scan Ultrasound
content: Vitreous hemorrhage or dense asteroid hyalosis

sections.title: The IOL Master Process
content: Step 1: Patient alignment to the chinrest; fixate on the internal target.
Step 2: Dual-beam emission to measure axial length (AL) from tear film to RPE.
Step 3: Automated keratometry using 6 spots in a hexagonal pattern.
Step 4: White-to-White (WTW) measurement for anterior segment evaluation.
Step 5: Automated calculation using SRK/T, Holladay 2, or Barrett Universal II formulas.

sections.title: Gold Standard: Immersion vs. Contact
content: Immersion Technique: Use a Prager shell filled with BSS; avoids direct pressure on the globe, decreasing error by ~0.15mm.
Contact Technique: Risk of corneal indentation leading to artifactual shortening of the AL by up to 0.5mm, causing hyperopic shift.
Standardized Velocity: Always confirm 1550 m/s in phakic eyes. Use 1532 m/s for aphakic and 1532 m/s for pseudophakic eyes.
Signal Quality: Ensure clear retinal spike with 80-100% gain.

content.explanation: O: Optical is best (IOL Master); I: Immersion is second; L: Least precise is contact (Log/Applanation).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: A 1mm error in AL measurement results in a ~2.5D error in IOL power calculation.
Always compare eyes: AL difference between two eyes should typically be <0.3mm.
Refractive Surprise: Always re-verify biometry if the calculated IOL power differs by >1.0D from the predicted emmetropic power.
Modern Formula Evolution: Shift from regression formulas (SRK II) to vergence-based formulas (Barrett, Hill-RBF, Haigis) to account for effective lens position (ELP).
